points: His mother's brethren spake of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem, whispering for their nephew, and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, He is our brother. They chose him by kinship, not by righteousness.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: With that money Abimelech hired vain and light persons, wicked and empty men, which followed him.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: All the men of Shechem and all the house of Millo gathered together and made Abimelech king by the plain of the pillar that was in Shechem. They endorsed the man who had just used their money and his hired men to murder his seventy brothers.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Jotham applied the parable: if ye have done truly and sincerely in that ye have made Abimelech king, and if ye have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, then rejoice ye in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: He reminded them of what they owed his father: my father fought for you, and adventured his life far, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian; and ye are risen up against my father's house this day, and have slain his sons, threescore and ten persons upon one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother. They did it only because he was kin to them.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the men of Shechem and the house of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem and from the house of Millo, and devour Abimelech. That is what the parable of the bramble was about: he prophesied that they would destroy one another, and it came to pass.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Jotham ran away and fled to Beer and dwelt there, for fear of Abimelech his brother. His brother already had a reputation for killing; he knew he could be next.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: When Abimelech had reigned three years over Israel, God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech. Read that carefully: the Lord sent the evil spirit. When somebody's spirit suddenly changes toward you, we tend to think it is just that person; the scripture shows the Most High is the one who stirs these things.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: The reason is given: that the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren. The hired men and the backers carried the blood guilt too. Abimelech ran for three years and everything looked good, but you are not getting away with evil.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: The men of Shechem set liers in wait for him in the top of the mountains, and they robbed all that came along that way by them; and it was told Abimelech. The treachery the Most High sent had begun.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Gaal the son of Ebed came with his brethren and went over to Shechem, and the men of Shechem put their confidence in him. They went out into the fields, gathered their vineyards, trode the grapes, made merry, went into the house of their god, did eat and drink, and cursed Abimelech.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Gaal talked big: who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? is not he the son of Jerubbaal? and Zebul his officer? serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem: for why should we serve him? He asked why they should be serving this Israelite at all.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Would to God this people were under my hand! then would I remove Abimelech. He was talking cash money with wine in him: increase thine army, and come out.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: When Zebul the ruler of the city, Abimelech's officer, heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger was kindled. He sent messengers unto Abimelech privily, saying, Behold, Gaal and his brethren fortify the city against thee.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Abimelech and all the people with him rose up by night and laid wait against Shechem in four companies. When Gaal saw the people coming down from the top of the mountains, Zebul told him, Thou seest the shadow of the mountains as if they were men, playing him until it was too late.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Then Zebul threw his own words back at him: where is now thy mouth, wherewith thou saidst, Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him? is not this the people that thou hast despised? go out, I pray now, and fight with them. All of that big talk disappeared when the fight showed up.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Gaal went out before the men of Shechem and fought with Abimelech, and Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many were overthrown and wounded, even unto the entering of the gate. Abimelech dwelt at Arumah, and Zebul thrust out Gaal and his brethren, that they should not dwell in Shechem.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Abimelech fought against the city all that day; he took the city, slew the people that was therein, beat down the city, and sowed it with salt.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Abimelech gat him up to mount Zalmon, cut down a bough from the trees with an axe, laid it on his shoulder, and said unto the people that were with him, What ye have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done. They cut every man his bough, put them to the hold, and set the hold on fire upon them, so that all the men of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Then went Abimelech to Thebez, and there was a strong tower within the city, and all the men and women of the city fled to the top of it. Abimelech came unto the tower and went hard unto the door to burn it with fire, and a certain woman cast a piece of a millstone upon Abimelech's head, and all to brake his skull. A millstone is a heavy stone; it crushed his skull.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: Thus God rendered the wickedness of Abimelech, which he did unto his father, in slaying his seventy brethren; and all the evil of the men of Shechem did God render upon their heads. Both sides were judged; for three years they reigned and everything looked good, then the Most High brought the judgment.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

points: After Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, a man of Issachar; he judged Israel twenty and three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

cases.name: Abimelech son of Gideon
cases.charge: Slaying his seventy brethren upon one stone with silver out of the house of Baal-berith; making himself king at Shechem
cases.preview: Gideon’s son by his concubine in Shechem went to his mother’s kin and told them to remember he was their own flesh and blood, and they chose him by kinship rather than by righteousness.
